title: When Perception Collides with Priors: Diagnosing Modal Polarization in Video Understanding Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.26972v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong video comprehension, largely benefiting from extensive training on realistic video data. However, when video perception severely conflicts with internal priors or common sense, we identify a critical failure pattern termed Modal Polarization, where models fail to integrate modalities and instead bifurcate into two distinct extremes: Cognitive Inertia, where models rigidly adhere to priors despite contradictory visual evidence, and Perceptual Inertia, where they blindly trust video perception while ignoring logical inconsistencies. To investigate this, we introduce TheaterBench, a benchmark designed to expose Modal Polarization using counter-intuitive scenarios that violate physical laws or common sense - situations rarely encountered in standard training distributions. Extensive experiments reveal that current state-of-the-art (SOTA) models exhibit severe Modal Polarization,

translated_title: 当感知与先验冲突时：诊断视频理解模型中的模态极化现象
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在视频理解方面取得了强大的能力，这主要得益于在真实视频数据上的广泛训练。然而，当视频感知与内部先验或常识发生严重冲突时，我们发现了一种关键的失败模式，称之为“模态极化”，即模型无法整合各模态信息，而是分裂为两个截然不同的极端：认知惯性——模型尽管存在矛盾的视觉证据仍僵化地坚持先验；以及感知惯性——模型盲目信任视频感知而忽视逻辑上的不一致。为了研究这一现象，我们引入了TheaterBench，一个旨在通过违反物理定律或常识的反直觉场景来揭示模态极化的基准测试——这类场景在标准训练数据分布中很少出现。大量实验表明，当前最先进的模型表现出严重的模态极化现象。
tldr: 该论文揭示了多模态大语言模型在视频感知与先验常识冲突时会出现“模态极化”失败模式（分为认知惯性与感知惯性两种极端），并构建了基于反直觉场景的TheaterBench基准来系统诊断这一问题。
